title: '' == null is true but '' === null is false, so the strict check inside the loose guard is not redundant

ground_truth.statement: In PHP 8, comparing null with a non-empty string is false and comparing it with '' is true, while '' === null is false. Inside the `$value == null` branch the value can therefore be '', so the inner `$value === null` has a reachable false outcome and the code behind it runs.

allowed.reason: Mago reports these two codes for any loose comparison whose operand may be null, and its own test suite expects them: crates/analyzer/tests/cases/flow_loose_eq_null.php expects `possibly-null-operand` and `null-operand` for `if ($v == null)` on a `null|int` parameter, and issue_1757.php expects `possibly-null-operand` for `$i == 0` on `?int`. Intended output, not a claim about this fixture. The redundant-condition reports on line 15 are a different matter and stay counted.

notes: The loose-null guard is a legacy defensive pattern. A tool that treats `== null` like `=== null` reports the inner check as redundant and the branch as dead; the runtime script shows both are alive. The '0' sample is a deliberate control: PHP 8 tightened string-to-null comparison, so '0' == null is false and must not enter the outer branch. The finding is independently corroborated by the still-open upstream report PR 2579 (https://github.com/carthage-software/mago/pull/2579), which describes the same root cause; the runtime proof here was derived from the fixture first.
